text:
The morbid lullaby, now not just a hum but a resonating chord, tuned the very air around David. A deep, internal tremor pulsed from *within* the cabin’s structure, a sustained, low-frequency oscillation emanating from what felt like six kilometers beneath his feet. It wasn’t a random shake, but a calculated vibration, hitting a cold, precise frequency: 4.71 cycles per second, designed to unravel. The air grew dense, metallic with ozone, as if an immense, unseen machine had just powered on for its initial debut, a grand, horrifying entrance into a market of souls.

The whispers, which had just spoken of “architects repaid,” now shifted, becoming slicker, more predatory. They spoke of “liquidation events” and “hostile acquisitions,” of “market adjustments” and the “unfettered capital” of the deep. The hum around him seemed to solidify, creating a visible shimmer in the air, a faint, almost imperceptible iridescence that pulsed to the rhythm of the new tremor. It was the full unveiling of the Undertow’s financial might, and he was standing in the very heart of its inaugural trading floor. The ‘7297.49’ wasn’t just a number on a clock; it was the frequency of the new world, the specific pitch of its terrible, unfolding song. A hairline crack spiderwebbed across a previously untouched section of wall, not from age, but from the inside out, a testament to the internal pressure of this grand, awful enterprise.
